data.body:
The new reentry guard (`existing_span is not None and existing_span.is_recording(): span = existing_span`) is restricted to `info.operation_type is OperationType.CONTEXT`. For a STEP attempt, execution always falls into the `else` branch and calls `_start_span(...)`, which (unchanged by this PR) unconditionally does `self._operation_spans[registry_key] = span`, silently overwriting whatever recording span was previously registered under that same attempt key.

This is exactly the "timed in-process resume re-enters the same operation" scenario the docstring on `_attach_context` describes generically (not CONTEXT-specific), and that this PR explicitly fixes for CONTEXT here and for *every* span type (including attempts) in `ExecutionOtelPlugin._start_span`, which now ends+marks a stale recording span (`durable.span.replaced_on_reentry`) before replacing it. Here, a re-entered STEP attempt's previous span is dropped from the registry without ever calling `.end()` on it, so it is never exported — a real telemetry gap distinct from the context-scope leak `_attach_context` already prevents.

Extend the `is_recording()` reuse check to STEP attempts too (or better, move an equivalent "end the stale recording span before replacing it" check into `_start_span` itself so every caller benefits), and add a test mirroring `test_reentered_step_attempt_releases_the_previous_scope` (added for `ExecutionOtelPlugin` in this PR) for `InvocationOtelPlugin`.
